annotations.title: Plan and usage for this key

description: What this API key is entitled to and how much of it has been used: the plan, the field tier that decides how much of a lookup answer comes back, the requests counted so far, the allowance, and when it resets. Use it to explain why a field is missing from a lookup, or before a large batch. Usage counts against the anniversary of the subscription rather than the calendar month, and can lag a few seconds behind. A null `hard_limit` means we never stop serving - it is NOT a limit of zero.
name: my_entitlement

apikey.description:
The credential itself. The key is never echoed - only its id, which is
what the console shows and what you can act on.

allowed_cidrs.description:
The source addresses this key may be used from. EMPTY means
unrestricted, never "deny all".

expires.description: Null for a key with no end date, which is the normal case.

org_id.description: The organization the key belongs to.

key.description: The plan the organization is on.

tier.description:
The field tier, which decides how much of a lookup answer comes
back. What each tier includes is documented on the lookup endpoint
rather than repeated here, so there is one place it can be wrong.

hard_limit.description:
Where we stop serving. NULL means never, which is the normal state
of an uncapped paid plan and is not the same as zero. Above the
quota and below this, requests are served and billed as overage.

quota.description: What the plan includes. Zero on a plan that includes none.

requests.description:
Requests counted in the current window. The same number the lookup
API gates on, and it can lag by a few seconds.

window_start.description: When the current allowance period began.
